findings.reason: the plan must state why extending the composer is insufficient, or §2 becomes a forked name-producer whose disagreement with the composer is the very thing §2 then measures.
findings.text: the plan proposes Jev grammar-slot selection as a cross-check "beside the composer" but does not say why the composer itself cannot be constrained to the closed vocabulary; the composer already renders through ISN and round-trip-validates its tokens (imas_codex/standard_names/grammar_adapter.py:144 compose_canonical_ir, imas_codex/standard_names/error_siblings.py:236 ISN round-trip), so the honest change may be to tighten the composer's own slot choice, not to add a parallel selector

findings.reason: naming the owner turns §3 into an extension (add a wrong-target predicate to the existing reference extractor) instead of a parallel link checker that drifts from doc_links.
findings.text: §3 adds link-label checking (deterministic self-link detection plus a Jev wrong-neighbour judgment) without naming the module that already owns link analysis: find_name_references resolves standard-name references and link targets, and imas_codex/standard_names/docs_gates.py:485 _links_are_hygienic already gates link syntax from it; the plan should extend find_name_references / the docs_gates link gate rather than open a second link reader

findings.reason: a Jev selector added beside families.select_anchor forks the anchor owner and drifts the docs prompt and harmonize command, which the current design avoids by sharing one function.
findings.text: §7 states select_anchor "in imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py picks it by heuristic", but select_anchor is defined in families.py:479 and imported into harmonize.py:32, and it already selects by the highest reviewer_score_docs among accepted members (not a bare heuristic); the plan should replace that rule inside families.select_anchor rather than add a Jev selector that harmonize's five call sites (harmonize.py:270, 291, 381, 435, 595) would have to choose between

findings.reason: dropping an already-existing deliverable removes a redundant node and records the guard's real location.
findings.text: §4's done-when asks for "A test shows the embedding order survives a failed rerank", but that guarantee is built into rerank_pool and already covered by test_rerank_pool_keeps_the_pool_order_when_every_judgement_fails (test_judgment.py:207) and by test_a_failed_batch_returns_the_embedding_order_with_a_note (tests/llm/test_search_tools.py:2483); the item should cite the existing test, not propose it as new work

response_events.reason: section 2 is the unwired measurement that decides whether the composer's slot choice should be constrained: its rule, fixed before the run, selects cross-check (the composer stays sole producer, Jev only flags) or generator (Jev's per-slot choice replaces the composer's own); no parallel producer is deployed by this section

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 hides the closed-vocabulary beam walk and the ISN rendering behind a single Choice-per-slot interface, which is behaviour larger than the interface it exposes.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 and §7 each propose a mechanism whose owner already exists in the repo (doc_links.py for link analysis; families.select_anchor for anchor selection) without naming either owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be, while §2/§4/§7 add public judgment fragments and change the behaviour of the existing `sn harmonize` command.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names the mechanisms it extends (rerank_pool in discovery/base/judgment.py, select_anchor, the composer, dd_domain_classifier.py); the owners it did not open (doc_links, families) are reported under duplicate_owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 adds a Jev segment selector "beside the composer" without stating why the composer, which already renders and validates through ISN, cannot be constrained instead.
